endorsements.quote: As prioritized by our stakeholders, a responsible AI framework should be nimble enough to allow quick but thorough reviews of AI solutions that have a low chance of causing any harm to an individual or the organization.
As the first step in FAIR-AI, an AI solution needs to go through an intake process.
For our health system, all AI solutions designated as high risk are escalated to the AI Governance committee where they undergo a multidisciplinary discussion.
Implemented AI solutions need continuous monitoring as they may fail to adapt to new data or practice changes, which can lead to inaccurate results and increasing bias over time 40 , 41 .
For these reasons, FAIR-AI requires a monitoring plan for every deployed AI solution consisting of an attestation by the business owner at regular intervals.
Individual leaders who are responsible for the deployment of AI solutions within the enterprise are designated as business owners; for clinical solutions, the business owner is a clinical leader.
Successful implementation requires support from institutional leadership, along with the allocation of resources to maintain documentation, manage new requests, and ensure proper monitoring.
By establishing formal review criteria and a consistent risk assessment process, institutions can ensure well-documented, defensible recommendations.

unlisted_practices: Require an AI Label and periodic end-user education for all AI solutions categorized as high risk.
Design implementation workflows that create transparency (alert, disclaimer, or consent) where end-users could be unaware they are interacting with AI.
Notify patients when AI is being used and, when appropriate, obtain their consent, particularly in sensitive or high-stakes situations.
Empower screening team members to reject AI requests that lack adequate documentation for a thorough review.
Review and update the AI governance framework regularly, at least annually, given rapid technology and regulatory change.
Provide training for AI evaluators and end-users.
Require clear and defensible justification for including predictor variables historically associated with discrimination.
Assess whether an AI system is equally accessible to those who may benefit.
Adopt a two-step review with a low-risk screening pathway and an in-depth review for solutions failing the screen.
Have business owners submit an intake form covering the problem, intended use, benefits, risks including worst-case scenarios, development and validation evidence, and FDA status.
Endorse AI guiding principles and an AI ethics statement at the highest level of the organization.
Maintain an AI inventory tool as a single source of truth catalog enabling accountability for review, monitoring, and transparency.
Emphasize human oversight and education on limitations and risks when AI transparency is lacking, particularly for generative AI.

screen.reason: The paper presents a practical governance framework (FAIR-AI) providing prescriptive guidance and resources for health systems to evaluate and monitor AI solutions.
